WV11-P01.5.note: Pressing every cap for wobble, warning that the wall needs a month to settle, and checking the rope twice at night all show unease that the new wall might not hold, with no ironic or teasing reading available.

exclusions.D: "The equinox tide comes in three days, and it will run higher than any tide we have seen here."

WV11-P02.5.note: Read literally, Varne's reply is a plain warning that the coming tide will run higher than any yet seen, and he backs it by doubling the stake, which shows worry; nothing in it reads as dry or teasing, and Pell's question is a reasonable one that gives no cause for irritation.
